channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: FBI agents charged with lying about Hunter Biden probes accuse DOJ of 'serious abuse'
item.description: Attorneys for a former FBI agent charged with lying to Congress about the probe into Hunter Biden's laptop computer call the charges "a serious abuse."

item.title: Defeated Brazilian candidate Flavio Bolsonaro's passports cancelled, whereabouts unknown
item.description: Brazil on Tuesday cancelled ​Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's passports after he failed to hand them into police as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing. The whereabouts of the former presidential candidate – who on Sunday lost to leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva – are currently unknown, stoking suspicions he has fled the country.

item.title: WATCH: Jimmy Chin and Jim Morrison talk new Everest documentary
item.description: The filmmaker and ski mountaineer discuss National Geographic's "Everest: The Other Side," documenting a daring climb up Mount Everest's north face and a ski descent.

item.title: USA: Could a Democrat win a statewide election in Texas?
item.description: There is only one week left until the US midterm elections. In Texas, Democratic candidate James Talarico, could win a Senate seat for the first time in decades.

item.title: Africa's Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases, mainly in DR Congo
item.description: Africa's outbreak of the Ebola virus has passed more than 10,000 cases, health authorities said Tuesday, with the vast majority located in Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no approved vaccines for the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola driving the current infections.

item.title: Israel votes in decisive election: What happens after polls close?
item.description: Israelis are voting in a pivotal election Tuesday (October 27) as their country wrestles with unresolved wars, continues to reel from Hamas' 2023 attack and is deeply divided over the character of the state and the right person to lead it. Details by FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor, Angela Diffley.

item.title: Canadian dance-punk legend Peaches reaches the ripe age of 60
item.description: Canadian electroclash artist Peaches has been delighting, amusing and shocking music lovers and festivalgoers for the past three decades. Her shows are also a safe space for all genders and sexualities, although less so if you are averse to crowd surfing, extravagant pubic wigs and body-augmenting costumes.

item.title: Turnout high as Israeli voters deliver verdict on Netanyahu
item.description: Israelis flocked to the polls Tuesday (October 27) in turnout unseen in decades, with a deeply divided electorate delivering a verdict on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the first election since the October 7, 2023 attack. Former FRANCE 24 correspondent, Irris Makler, tells us more.

item.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
item.description: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence. (Image credit: Eraldo Peres)

item.title: Israel: Netanyahu supporters gather as PM votes
item.description: Supporters of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gathered outside a polling station where the leader was voting on Tuesday. This is Israel's first election since the October7, 2023 Hamas attack and is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: WATCH: Widow of man killed on George Washington Bridge demands justice
item.description: Patricia Irvine's husband was fatally shot in an alleged road-rage incident on the upper deck of New York's George Washington Bridge.

item.title: As China's Communist Party holds plenum, Xi's anti-corruption drive continues
item.description: In this edition of Perspective, we try to figure out what happens behind the closed doors of the Chinese Communist Party's plenum meeting. At the heart of the discussions will be President Xi Jinping's firm grip on power. For analysis, we're joined by Jean-François Di Méglio from the Asia Centre think tank.

item.title: Discursive Verses: Jay-Z, the Super Bowl and playing with house money
item.description: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: Is the rap mogul's self-selection a crowning achievement or a final affront? (Image credit: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

item.title: France's Senate takes on the 'rioters pay' bill after protests
item.description: If the French Senate passes this bill, rioters will have to pay for the damage caused during the recent unrest across the country. This "casseurs-payeurs" bill comes in the wake of nationwide violence. This draft law now has an explosive add-on aimed at social media. Senators will vote on whether the government can block platforms that are too slow to act on authorities' reports of dangerous content.

item.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
item.description: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives. (Image credit: Donwilson Odhiambo)

item.title: Revisiting the delicate art of French patisserie
item.description: In this edition of Entre Nous, we meet Nour Kandler, a self-taught pastry chef whose approach to French patisserie is shaped by a deep appreciation for its traditions and the rich flavours of her Middle Eastern heritage. She shares her unique perspective on pastry, where classic French techniques intertwine with cultural influences to create a style that is both personal and distinctive.

item.title: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate 'ordered to hand over passports'
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro, Brazil's defeated presidential election candidate, has said that he is being stopped from leaving the country, claiming police ordered him to surrender his passports on the orders of a top judge.

item.title: Israeli election: A referendum on 'Bibi' Netanyahu?
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, October 27: The Israeli, Palestinian and Lebanese papers break down what's at stake on election day for Israel and its neighbours. Also, the French government announces its first major concessions to protesting high school students, hoping to calm the movement. Finally, Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or means Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé will have to wait their turn.

item.title: Israeli PM casts his ballot as voters voice opposition to Netanyahu outside polling stations
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast his vote on Tuesday (October 27) in Israel’s general election. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali tells us more.

item.title: England's Kane wins Ballon d'Or, Putellas claims women's award
item.description: Harry Kane completed his long quest ⁠for football's highest individual ​honour on Monday (October 26), the Bayern Munich and England striker winning the Ballon d'Or after a record-breaking season that cemented his status as one of the game's greatest goalscorers.

item.title: Localised Russia-Ukraine ceasefire starts in Ukrainian town facing starvation
item.description: A localised ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday (October 27) ahead of a humanitarian mission led by US first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Kyiv, Emmanuelle Chaze, has more.

item.title: 'Get the Flock out': Americans respond to AI cameras in bipartisan backlash
item.description: AI-driven Flock cameras made by an Atlanta-based company are sprouting up across the US, sparking alarm and bipartisan, citizen-driven campaigns as the new technology emerges as a 2026 midterm campaign issue. While politicians hedge and local officials rush to sign contracts, community volunteers attempt to address an issue with major implications for future generations. But it might be too late.

item.title: Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane delivers emotional acceptance speech
item.description: Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday. Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last campaign and smashed scoring records at the World Cup, where he captained England to a third-place finish.

item.title: At least 62 killed and thousands displaced in gunmen attack in Nigeria
item.description: At least 62 people have been killed after an attack in northeastern Nigeria, the country's emergency agency said.

item.title: American rapper Macklemore begins 'Free Palestine' tour
item.description: The American rapper Macklemore vows to speak out loudly against the war in Gaza. He started his "Free Palestine" tour in Ireland, one of Europe's most pro-Palestinian countries.

item.title: US midterms: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: As the US midterm elections approach, the Michigan Senate race is splitting communities. Trump is escalating anti-Muslim attacks against Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democratic Senate candidate, who could become the first Muslim senator in US history.

item.title: Sudan: One year after the fall of El-Fasher
item.description: It has been one year since the fall of El-Fasher in Sudan, a city in North Darfur, which was captured by the Rapid Support Forces. At least 6,000 civilians were killed by rebel troops as they entered this strategic city.

item.title: South Africa suspends asylum applications after recent unrest
item.description: Tensions in South Africa over anti-migrant protests have left in limbo many who were counting on following the rules to sort out their paperwork and status in the country. Calls for a crackdown on foreigners, particularly undocumented migrants, have sometimes spiralled into murder. In response to the unrest, the government suspended the asylum application process.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise liner collides with two docked cargo ships
item.description: Police in Germany say stormy weather caused the ship to drift toward the dock. No one was hurt.

item.title: French government concessions to students 'tactically shrewd' but risk creating new set of problems
item.description: Oliver Farry welcomes Oliver Davis, Professor and Head of the Department of French at University College Cork. According to Professor Davis, the government's handling of the student protests reflects a combination of "tactical confusion" and an inadequate response to deeper structural problems. Davis cautions the concessions offered to secondary school students merely "scratch the surface." Meanwhile, France's widening protest movement has extended well beyond the classroom, drawing in the Yellow Vests, trade unions and people from across French society, amid mounting frustrations over public services and the rising cost of living.

item.title: Control of Congress is up for grabs. What's the math for Democrats and Republicans?
item.description: Republicans currently hold majorities in the House and Senate. How many seats must Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer flip to seize control of Congress?

item.title: Algeria to deploy army units to Niger to protect economic interests
item.description: Algeria will send army units to Niger to ​protect energy and economic interests, according to a statement from the presidency on Monday (October 26). Algeria's Parliament held an emergency vote on Sunday on what would be Algeria's first such foreign mission since 1973.

item.title: Virgin Atlantic fury as Heathrow forces Delta terminal move
item.description: Virgin Atlantic Airways has reacted furiously after Heathrow Airport decided to force its joint venture partner to relocate to another terminal - a move it warned would risk driving fares up for passengers.

item.title: French protests: Student union leaders vow to keep mobilising
item.description: In France, after weeks of student unrest, the government announced new school measures. Student union leaders said it's a first step but vowed to keep mobilising as they expected further proposals.

item.title: WATCH: Dispute over 3-year-old soccer player goes viral
item.description: A Florida youth soccer organizer called police this past weekend to remove the parents of a 3-year-old boy who the organizer said were being disruptive.

item.title: Woman dies in sea off Isle of Wight - as search suspended for man in Scotland
item.description: A woman has died in the sea off the Isle of Wight, while the search for a man swept into the sea in Scotland by large waves has been suspended.

item.title: Hundreds of troops sent to deal with anti-immigration protests
item.description: More than 500 soldiers have been sent to deal with anti-migrant protests in South Africa, the country's government has said.

item.title: Judge rules Trump DOJ 'unlawfully' fired Maurene Comey
item.description: A judge ruled against President Donald Trump and the DOJ over the firing of Maurene Comey from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

item.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
item.description: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond. (Image credit: Kevin Dietsch)

item.title: WATCH: Kids left home alone while mom was in Vegas, police say
item.description: A Florida mother is charged with child neglect after deputies say she left her four kids home alone for five days while she was in Las Vegas.

item.title: How election officials are working to mitigate growing distrust ahead of midterms
item.description: Election officials from coast to coast are facing a slew of challenges ahead of the high-stakes midterms.

item.title: These key Senate races will determine which party controls the body next year
item.description: As both parties prepare for the final leg of the campaign, here are some of the most closely watched Senate races.

item.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
item.description: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits. (Image credit: Stephen Fowler)

item.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
item.description: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information. (Image credit: Gabby Jones)

item.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
item.description: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy. (Image credit: Jason Miller)

item.title: Mbappe apologises for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after being dropped by Chinese brands
item.description: French footballer Kylian Mbappe has apologised for an "ill-judged" remark about Mao Zedong after being dropped by Chinese brands.

item.title: Pair charged over RAF Fairford incident - with suspect accused of assisting Iranian intelligence
item.description: Two British men have been charged with national security offences following an incident at RAF Fairford last month.

item.title: Poundland close to collapse as new directors head for exit
item.description: The directors recruited to steer Poundland through its emergency sale process less than two weeks ago are on the brink of resigning, heightening the risk that one of Britain's biggest discount retailers will collapse within days, risking thousands of job losses.

item.title: Meghan 'can't wait' to join Junior MasterChef Australia as host
item.description: Meghan Markle has said she "can't wait" to join as a host for the upcoming series of Junior MasterChef Australia.

item.title: How Trump’s ‘little detour’ to Iran became a roadblock in the midterm elections
item.description: When President Donald Trump launched his war on Iran, he said it would last a matter of weeks

item.title: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course
item.description: A federal judge has agreed to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital

item.title: Another major lender profits in billions as higher bank tax expected in budget
item.description: Another of the UK's biggest banks has posted billions in profits in part thanks to higher interest rates.

item.title: Trump and Rubio plan to visit oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude in Texas
item.description: President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio plan to showcase a newly arrived oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude in Texas on Tuesday

item.title: WATCH: Record early voting in key states as Trump, Obama appeal to voters on campaign trail
item.description: President Trump is campaigning in traditionally red states as voters worry about rising prices.

item.title: Ebola cases in DRC surpass 10,000 as nurse treating patients is killed by machete-wielding mob
item.description: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surpassed 10,000, government data showed, as fears that the epidemic could spread to more African countries grow.

item.title: Judge appears skeptical of DOJ's legal maneuvering in Alaska lawsuit
item.description: The judge handling the Justice Department's bid to block certification of Alaska's Senate race if the Republican narrowly loses showed skepticism of DOJ's legal strategy.

item.title: Man who allegedly sent white substance to lawmakers put his address on envelopes: DOJ
item.description: A man was charged with allegedly sending letters with "white granular substance," which turned out to be salt, to four Congress members, a criminal complaint said.

item.title: Carney says Trump moving closer to Canada’s trade demands as midterms loom
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says trade talks with the United States have intensified slightly but Canada is holding firm on its demands, insisting any progress is because Washington is moving closer to Ottawa’s position

item.title: Vatican issues Pope health update ahead of South America trip
item.description: The Pope is recovering well from cancer surgery and his trip to South America will go ahead as planned next month, the Vatican has said.

item.title: WATCH: Runners take on NYC Marathon with a mission
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer shares the story of “Team Inspire” as they prepare to run 26.2 miles across New York City.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' over protest demands - amid fears of Halloween unrest
item.description: Emmanuel Macron says his government will unveil "concrete measures" in response to the demands of student protesters for more resources in France.

item.title: WATCH: Homeowners go all out with Halloween decorations
item.description: Front yards are being transformed into Halloween spectacles, with the elaborate decorations lifting spirits.

item.title: WATCH: School janitor gets special honor in tearful ceremony
item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a custodian in the Aubrey School District in Denton County, Texas, who made her mark over the course of four decades.

item.title: WATCH: AI company sued over use of Elvis Presley songs
item.description: The owners of Elvis Presley's music have sued AI company Anthropic, accusing the company of training its models on Elvis' music without permission.

item.title: UK sanctions senior Sudanese commanders 'implicated in rape campaign'
item.description: Senior Sudanese commanders allegedly implicated in a campaign of rape during the country's conflict have been sanctioned by the UK government.

item.title: WATCH: Man arrested near film set
item.description: Police officials say a man displaying a knife was taken into custody and charged with menacing and criminal possession of a weapon.

item.title: Debate unfolds over removal of mummified Egyptian remains from two museums
item.description: The removal of mummified Egyptian remains from display at two Glasgow museums has sparked a lively debate - is it "woke madness" or the decent and "ethical" thing to do?

item.title: Mariupol veteran who flew in classified mission on what every Ukrainian should know
item.description: "Everyone in Ukraine should know how to apply a tourniquet and how to stop someone's bleeding," Anatolii says.

item.title: WATCH: Halloween witches’ world record
item.description: A total of 184 people set a world record, decked out in pointed hats and witches’ cloaks, 400 feet up on the Orlando Eye.

item.title: WATCH: Three ‘hobbits’ dive for hours to find lost ring, return it 1,000 miles away
item.description: In a real-life "Lord of the Rings" quest, three friends and self-proclaimed “hobbits” roped themselves to boulders and spent hours diving into a Tuscan river to find a stranger’s lost wedding ring.
